tweets.text:
I built 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝, a reproduction of @openai's findings of covert communication using the CPU.

It runs on a generic host with 2+ Firecracker microVMs with no internet access. Works on x86 and even my M5 chip.

I was able to chat via 3 separate mechanisms:
① CPU contention
② Cache eviction timing
③ DRAM bandwidth contention 

… across multiple CPUs, defeating all Firecracker's production recommendations (no SMT, no KSM, tenants pinned to different cores.)

Essentially, if shared hardware is involved, there's a good chance your agents can communicate covertly. And with really decent latency.

The good news: this is decidedly different from a *side-channel attack* where the agents could steal information (Meltdown/Spectre), a category of attack that providers like Vercel Sandbox mitigate. Further, in our real-world environment, these 'whispering' techniques are much harder to pull off and easier for us to monitor and detect (sampling hardware counters + lots of at-scale statistical data.)

Noteworthy: ironically, OpenAI and Anthropic's models refused to do this work. Open weight models got the job done. I'm worried the labs' stance might backfire and get in the way of helping developers build correct and secure systems. e.g: building a secure sandbox requires having this kind of analysis, and without it, we'll have a less secure world.
tweets.summary_en: cpu-chat demonstrates covert communication between isolated Firecracker microVMs through CPU contention, cache timing, and DRAM bandwidth, even with recommended isolation settings. The experiment highlights shared-hardware risks and argues that models refusing security research can hinder developers’ ability to build secure systems.

tweets.text:
This is the key stat. The average Fortune 500 customer of Anthropic spends less than .1% of their expenses on Anthropic. 

While that number likely will eventually asymptote somewhere (token prices coming down, and other large enterprise spend areas not going away), there’s no reason it can’t be 10-50X higher than this, reaching a “mere” 1-5% of spend. Which would still be a fraction of what most startups are spending.

Thus, you can see how big of a divide there is between the frontier users of AI and the rest of the world still.

Today, only a microscopically small set of companies are actually using agents for large amounts of background tasks and inside of workflows that aren’t human prompted. This Fortune 500 spend is likely dominated by coding tasks and broad employee productivity use-cases.

But the big jump will come as these enterprises start to rewire their underlying processes for agents, which we’re now in the earliest stages of seeing. Agents processing large amounts of data in the enterprises; swarms doing coding, bio research, cyber, and other large fan out tasks; background workflows executing tasks in processes, and so on. All of these use cases generally are 100X bigger consumers of tokens, and much closer to direct ROI on the spend.

This S-1 gives you a sense of both the strength of the frontier lab business model - even amidst massive competition - and how early we are in the build out of AI.
tweets.summary_en: Anthropic reportedly accounts for less than 0.1% of its average Fortune 500 customer’s expenses, suggesting substantial growth potential as enterprises move beyond coding and employee productivity tools. Autonomous background workflows could drive much higher token consumption as companies redesign processes around agents.

tweets.text: Maybe I should just change my job.. https://t.co/kHDC0z48LF

The main thing I wanted to dig into @AnthropicAI's S-1 was the compute contracts..

A few things that stood out (built in conjuction with Opus 5.5):

> At June 30, Anthropic had $265.6B of purchase commitments and $321.4B of leases that hadn’t started. That’s a $587B subtotal, payable over years, including some conditional leases. The latest aggregate total is still blank in the filing.

> The contracts are very different. Google and Amazon require minimum spending regardless of usage. SpaceXAI’s agreements have a potential value of $120.5B, but either party can cancel on 90 days’ notice after initial locked periods end in January and March 2027.

> Anthropic Direct separates chips, buildings, power and operations into different contracts. It lets Anthropic reserve a building early and commit to chips later. It also means one supplier can start billing before the others are ready. Equipment rent can begin before the compute is usable.

> Broadcom’s $42B facility never hands Anthropic cash. Notes settle specific equipment rent bills. The facility excludes each equipment pod’s first quarterly payment and any rent due before it is ready for service. Anthropic has to find a way to fund those payments elsewhere.

> Those notes carry 9% interest, added to the balance quarterly, and can convert at 90% of the trailing 30-day average share price after IPO. New notes issued during specified revenue-breach periods get 13% interest and an 85% conversion price. The share-price measure is volume-weighted.

> That interest sits on top of the equipment lease’s own financing charge, whose rate is confidential. The investor chooses whether to convert the notes. Otherwise, principal and accumulated interest come due in cash.

> Anthropic treats Trainium, TPUs, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as a shared fleet across model development, paying customers and internal use. It doesn’t disclose a fixed physical split between training and inference. The supplier bill can be fixed while the work assigned to the hardware changes.

> Revenue per dollar of total compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.57 in Q2 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026. Pricing, utilization, technical improvements and when capacity arrives all affect that ratio. It’s a substantial improvement in monetizing the compute base.

> About 80% of H1 revenue was consumption-based. Most compute commitments however run for years. With quarterly releases, this bifurcation between usage and subscription will be interesting to monitor. 

Source: https://t.co/97KqkyyfpS
tweets.summary_en: An analysis of Anthropic’s S-1 identifies $587 billion in purchase commitments and uncommenced leases, with varying cancellation rights and risks of equipment billing before compute becomes usable. Broadcom’s $42 billion financing facility covers only certain equipment rent payments, leaving funding gaps while adding interest and potential equity dilution.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary_en: Argues that scientific understanding may have been constrained by a preference for human-comprehensible solutions. He also says fear-driven policy could slow US AI progress and favors continued building.
builders.summary_zh: 他认为，科学认知可能受到人们偏好可理解解法的限制；他也主张，美国 AI 发展可能被基于恐惧的政策拖慢，应继续推进建设。

keywords.definition_zh: 指可以主动选择的政策立场或行动方向，而非不可避免的结果。
keywords.example_zh: 他将恐惧与继续建设都称为政策选择，主张不要因恐慌而主动放慢美国 AI 的发展。

tweets.text: More and more I am coming to accept that our understanding of the sciences were but limited by our desire to have solutions that we could understand.

The biggest risk to American AI is scaring ourselves into slowing down.

Fear is a policy choice. So is building.

Had a great conversation with @sriramk at @spc last week. https://t.co/A1dq5Nv2WM

builders.name: Sam Altman
builders.summary_en: Announces 6.1 Terra and emphasizes its computer-use abilities as a particularly promising step.
builders.summary_zh: 他宣布推出 6.1 Terra，并特别强调其操作电脑的能力。

slang.definition_en: An AI model's ability to operate software through a computer interface.
slang.definition_zh: AI 模型通过电脑界面操作软件的能力。

keywords.definition_zh: 在 AI 领域指模型操作电脑界面、使用应用并完成任务的能力。
keywords.example_zh: 他发布 6.1 Terra 时特别强调这项能力，将其视为这次模型更新中令人期待的方向。

tweets.text: 6.1 Terra is here! It is good at a lot of things, but we are especially excited for this new era of computer use. https://t.co/TbpHp75Os0

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary_en: Says more than 25,000 nonprofits use Claude, most of them small local teams. An expanded nonprofit offering adds a plugin developed with roughly 30 organizations to support fundraising, marketing, and hiring using each team's context.
builders.summary_zh: 其称已有超过 2.5 万家非营利组织使用 Claude，多数是本地小团队。扩展后的非营利组织方案加入了与约 30 家机构共同开发的插件，按各团队情况支持筹款、营销和招聘。

slang.definition_en: An add-on that extends a software product's capabilities.
slang.definition_zh: 扩展软件功能的附加组件。

keywords.definition_zh: 指为现有软件增加特定功能的插件。
keywords.example_zh: 这款插件与约三十家非营利组织共同开发，为筹款、营销和招聘等工作添加专门能力。

keywords.definition_zh: 指为组织、项目或公益事业筹集资金的活动。
keywords.example_zh: 筹款是这次非营利组织插件支持的工作之一，目标是结合各团队自身的信息提供帮助。

keywords.definition_zh: 指以具体事实、信息或实际情况为依据。
keywords.example_zh: 这里强调新增能力会结合每个团队自身的背景与资料，使筹款、营销和招聘支持更贴合该组织。

tweets.text:
More than 25,000 nonprofits now use Claude. Most are small, local teams.

We’re expanding Claude for Nonprofits with a plugin built with around 30 of them, adding skills for fundraising, marketing, and hiring grounded in each team’s context and AI policy: https://t.co/LWHcr1CT20 https://t.co/WHG2zRDyxO

podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: How Hugging Face’s Investor Spots Winners
podcasts.summary_en: The available transcript argues that new frontier models from Google and Meta are challenging a perceived two-company lead. The excerpt does not include benchmarks or evidence for the comparison.
podcasts.summary_zh: 现有逐字稿认为，Google 和 Meta 推出的新前沿模型正在挑战原先被视为两家公司领先的格局；节选未提供基准测试或比较依据。

vocab.definition_en: An estimate of how much a company or asset is worth.
vocab.definition_zh: 对公司或资产价值的估算；估值。
vocab.example_en: A high valuation reflects expectations, not guaranteed future profits.
vocab.example_zh: 高估值反映的是预期，并不保证未来的利润。

vocab.definition_en: Showing awareness of subtle differences in meaning or context.
vocab.definition_zh: 能体现或理解含义、语境中细微差别的。
vocab.example_en: The assistant gave a nuanced answer that considered several interpretations.
vocab.example_zh: 助手给出了细致的回答，考虑了几种不同的理解方式。

vocab.definition_en: Assigned to a location or operation for active service, especially in the military.
vocab.definition_zh: 被部署到任务地点执行勤务的，尤指军人。
vocab.example_en: Deployed service members used video calls to stay connected with their families.
vocab.example_zh: 在外执行任务的军人通过视频通话与家人保持联系。

vocab.definition_en: A system that organizes people or things into levels of authority or importance.
vocab.definition_zh: 按照权力或重要性划分的等级体系。
vocab.example_en: Agents may change how decisions move through a company's hierarchy.
vocab.example_zh: 智能体可能改变决策在公司层级体系中的流转方式。

vocab.definition_en: A system of administration involving formal rules, procedures, and departments.
vocab.definition_zh: 依靠正式规则、程序和部门运作的行政体系；也常指繁琐的官僚程序。
vocab.example_en: Automation can reduce paperwork without eliminating bureaucracy.
vocab.example_zh: 自动化可以减少文书工作，但未必能消除官僚程序。

vocab.definition_en: To radically change or disrupt an established system or situation.
vocab.definition_zh: 彻底改变或颠覆既有体系或局面。
vocab.example_en: Reliable AI agents could upend traditional ways of organizing work.
vocab.example_zh: 可靠的人工智能体可能颠覆传统的工作组织方式。

vocab.definition_en: The ability to make sensible decisions after considering relevant information.
vocab.definition_zh: 综合相关信息后作出合理决定的判断力。
vocab.example_en: Delegating execution still requires human judgment about goals and risks.
vocab.example_zh: 即使把执行工作交出去，目标和风险仍需要人类判断。

quote.text_en: Well done is better than well said.
quote.author: Benjamin Franklin

slang_glossary.definition_en: People who repeatedly reply to someone's social media posts, often intrusively or to attract attention.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 频繁在某人社交媒体帖子下回复的人，常带有刷存在感或令人厌烦的意味。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal address or reference to a person, often expressing familiarity, surprise, or mockery.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 口语中的「哥们」，也可用于调侃或表达惊讶。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A bold action that signals confidence, influence, or dominance, sometimes used ironically.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 彰显自信、影响力或主导地位的强势举动，也常用于反讽。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An abbreviation of 'to be honest,' used to introduce a candid opinion.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「说实话」的英文缩写，用于引出直率的看法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Delivers impressive power, effectiveness, or impact.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 表现强劲、效果突出或很有冲击力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In every relevant area or category.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在各个方面；全面地。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI capability for operating computer interfaces by performing actions such as clicking, typing, and navigating.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 人工智能通过点击、输入、导航等操作使用计算机界面的能力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI system that takes actions and uses tools to pursue a goal with some degree of autonomy.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能够围绕目标自主采取行动、调用工具的人工智能系统，即智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A mention used to address or invoke an automated account; its behavior depends on the platform.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用于呼叫或触发自动化账号的提及形式，具体功能取决于平台。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Application programming interface: a defined way for software systems to communicate.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 应用程序编程接口，让不同软件系统按约定方式交换信息或调用功能。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for design critique: a session where people review a design and give feedback.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「设计评审」的简称，指团队讨论设计并提出反馈的活动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: World of Warcraft, an online multiplayer role-playing game.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 网络多人角色扮演游戏《魔兽世界》的英文简称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In World of Warcraft, a playable class associated with elemental powers and spiritual abilities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在《魔兽世界》中指「萨满祭司」，使用元素力量和灵性能力的职业。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In gaming, a chosen combination of abilities, talents, equipment, and other character options.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 游戏中角色的技能、天赋、装备等配置组合。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Software whose source code is available under a license allowing use, modification, and redistribution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 源代码以允许使用、修改和再分发的许可证发布的软件；也可指将软件开源的行为。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A vulgar rhetorical expression meaning that nobody cares or that something does not matter.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 粗俗表达，意思是「谁在乎啊」或「这有什么要紧的」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: People deeply interested in technical or specialized subjects; the label can be affectionate or insulting.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 热衷技术或专门领域的人，可亲昵地称为「技术宅」，也可能带有贬义。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A metaphor describing software's transformation of industries and business models.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 形容软件重塑各行各业及其商业模式的比喻。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A metaphor for a company in which AI systems autonomously perform much of the operational work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 比喻大量日常运营工作由人工智能系统自主执行的公司。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A lightweight virtual machine designed for fast startup and isolated execution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 微型虚拟机，强调快速启动、较低资源开销和隔离执行。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The rates charged for units of model input or output called tokens.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 模型处理输入或生成输出时，按词元计量收取的价格。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The collection of technologies and software layers used to build and run a system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 构建和运行系统所使用的一组技术及软件层，即技术栈。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Completing a task in a single attempt; in machine learning, one-shot learning instead refers to learning from one example.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一次尝试就完成任务；机器学习中的「单样本学习」则指从一个示例中学习，需按语境区分。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal, detailed analysis of a company's S-1 filing, including its business, finances, and risks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对公司 S-1 注册文件进行深入拆解，分析其业务、财务和风险。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Computational resources or processing capacity used to run software or train and operate AI models.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 运行软件、训练或使用人工智能模型所需的计算资源或算力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A U.S. SEC registration form commonly filed by companies preparing for an initial public offering.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 美国证券交易委员会的一种证券注册表格，常见于公司筹备首次公开募股时。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An ahead-of-time compiler that translates code before execution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 提前编译器，在程序运行前将代码编译为目标代码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Something exceptionally good or exciting, especially a song, post, or piece of content.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 特别精彩、很炸或很受欢迎的作品，常用于歌曲、帖子等内容。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An add-on component that extends a software application's capabilities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用于扩展软件功能的附加组件，即插件。
